contradiction_discovered: The P2 probe classified a harness process that dies by a signal after DISPATCHED as HARNESS_FAILED -> UNRUNNABLE -> PROBE_UNRUNNABLE, owner ENVIRONMENT, retryable. A subject that ends its own process (os.abort, os.kill(getpid, SIGTERM)) was therefore charged to the environment budget and retried, which is exactly what INTERRUPT-SIG-2 forbids; the probe had no way to tell a signal it sent itself from one it did not send.

replacement.summary: After DISPATCHED the controller's own signal ledger decides, never the signal number. The ledger holds the signal: the controller stopped its own observation — an interruption, no ProbeResult, no verdict, no owner, closed through the P4 interruption path (OUTCOME_UNKNOWN once dispatched). The ledger does not hold it: EXECUTED + INDETERMINATE(NON_CONTROLLER_SIGNAL), routed INTEGRATION and never retried. Before DISPATCHED nothing changes: UNRUNNABLE / ENVIRONMENT (V2-002).

semantics.CASE A — after DISPATCHED, the controlle: an interruption: no ProbeResult, no BehaviorVerdict, no owner; the operation closes OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and the provenance is kept. It applies to whatever the harness managed to report: a cooperative SIGINT surfaces inside the subject as KeyboardInterrupt, and reading that as the subject's own behaviour would charge a controller's decision to the product (measured while implementing; the check therefore covers every post-dispatch path, not only a signal exit)
semantics.CASE B — after DISPATCHED, the ledger do: EXECUTED + INDETERMINATE(NON_CONTROLLER_SIGNAL); never UNRUNNABLE, never ENVIRONMENT, never a verdict, and never a global 'signal exit -> REFUTED'
semantics.CASE C — before DISPATCHED: the observation mechanism failed: UNRUNNABLE, owner ENVIRONMENT (V2-002, unchanged and unconditional — the owner decision states it without a provenance test)

f1_impact.verdict: AFFECTED — declared, and no format version bump is required
f1_impact.question: §6 of the owner decision: is IndeterminateReason serialized in an event payload, in an event schema, or in an F1 enum catalog used to interpret existing journals?

determined_mechanically.IndeterminateReason: NO. The payload enums of journal format 1 are ControlProjection, FailureCode, ObligationRole, Owner and StoryAdmissionDisposition (aisef2/journal/event.py SCHEMAS); format 2 adds Enforcement, IdentityGrade, OperationOutcome, ReleaseStatus, ResourceKind and SignalProvenance (aisef2/journal/format2.py). IndeterminateReason, BehaviorVerdict and ProbeResult appear nowhere under aisef2/journal, and F1's conformance catalog (F1.payload_enum.*) lists Vacuity, Relevance, AdequacyOutcome, TestExecutionStatus, TestOutcome and TestSelection. The new reason therefore touches F2's vocabulary, not F1's.
determined_mechanically.FailureCode: YES. failure/observed carries code: _enum(FailureCode), so the taxonomy is a typed enumeration carried in an event payload, and F1 freezes those. Adding NON_CONTROLLER_SIGNAL grows it, so F1 is declared affected.

compatibility: no existing member changes meaning, so no existing event is reinterpreted — the reason F1 freezes payload enums at all
no journal written before this amendment can contain the new value; old journals remain valid under their original format identity and read byte-identically
a reader that does not know the member refuses the event (fail closed), never misreads it
no new event type and no new payload field, so §35 requires no format version bump; the frozen compatibility mechanism (journal format 2) is unchanged and still reads format-1 journals

evidence_compatibility_impact.what_changes: The outcome of a post-dispatch signal: UNRUNNABLE/ENVIRONMENT (retryable) -> either an interruption with no result (the controller's own signal) or EXECUTED + INDETERMINATE(NON_CONTROLLER_SIGNAL) -> INTEGRATION, never retried. python_callable.py and probe/protocol.py change, so probe_digest changes and every spec bound to the old digest is refused (INVALID_SPEC, scenario D) until it is recompiled.
evidence_compatibility_impact.calibration: every ProbeCapabilityCalibration bound to the old digest is historical; calibration is re-established by execution for the new digest (never by copying a record and editing it)
evidence_compatibility_impact.evidence_written_under_the_old_wording: P1, P2 and P3 seals stay untouched and remain evidence of what those phases delivered under their then-current architecture identity. The current P2 evidence records that name the probe digest (P2-CALIBRATION.json, P2-PROBE-PROTOCOL.json) are recomputed; their before/after sha256 are recorded in closure-evidence/v2/P4-COMPLETION-CORRECTION-V2-003.json. V1 evidence is untouched.
evidence_compatibility_impact.unaffected: the Owner set (F3), ProbeExecutionStatus x BehaviorVerdict and the ContractSatisfaction derivation (F2), the Probe protocol members and signatures, ProbeResult fields, the two calibration contracts, subject-absence semantics (§10.2), PRECONDITION_ABSENT routing (V2-001), harness timeout vs subject deadline (§9.2, V2-002)

implementation_decisions_for_owner_revie: The probe digest covers probe/protocol.py and probe/python_callable.py, as before. The provenance mechanism it now uses (aisef2/runtime/process_range.py) is NOT in the digest: a P4 range fix would otherwise invalidate every product spec. The probe's use of it is visible in python_callable.py, which is in the digest.

The probe releases its own range in a finally block; a range that will not empty raises (RangeNotEmpty / RangeEscaped) rather than being swallowed, so a leak is never silent. A story may instead take ownership through the harness-owned on_range hook, which is not part of the frozen Probe protocol (PROBE-META-1).
CASE C is applied unconditionally, as the owner decision states it: a signal before DISPATCHED is UNRUNNABLE / ENVIRONMENT even when the controller's ledger holds it.
